lines: Probabilistic voice router: at each evaluation a draw picks which of its six channels pass their input to their output, from a weight per channel and a target number of active voices
Sets how many channels take part in the draw, counting from the first; 1 to 6, growing to 16 when an expander is linked
Sets how many voices should be active after each evaluation, in whole voices, capped by the number of tracks taking part
Crossfades the density between the TRACK DENS knob and the DENS CV jack: fully anticlockwise the knob alone, fully clockwise the voltage alone
Sets how far the voice count may wander from the density target: fully anticlockwise gives exactly that number, and turning clockwise widens a gaussian spread around it
Sets how many bars pass between evaluations: 1, 2, 4, 8 or 16
Sets the chance that an evaluation is passed over and the channels keep their current state, 0 for never and 1 for always
Sets how long a channel takes to fade up when it is switched on, 0 to 10 seconds; it applies to channels in F mode
Sets how long a channel takes to fade down when it is switched off, 0 to 10 seconds; it applies to channels in F mode
Sets that channel's weight in the draw, 0 for never chosen and 1 for most likely; the menu's crossfade mode raises the weight to a power before the draw
Crossfades that channel's weight between its PROB knob and its PROB CV jack: fully anticlockwise the knob alone, fully clockwise the voltage alone
Sets what that channel does when it is chosen: F fades its input up and down over the fade times, G switches it through at once, T sends a short pulse and passes nothing else
Counts beats on each rise above 1V; a bar is as many beats as the menu says, and an evaluation comes after the number of bars LENGTH sets
On a rising edge above 1V it either zeroes the bar count or forces an evaluation at once, whichever the Reset input mode menu is set to
Sets the target voice count, 0V to 10V covering none to all of the tracks taking part; how far it overrides the TRACK DENS knob is set by TRK DENS XFADE
Takes over the evaluation period while patched, 0V to 10V stepping through 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16 bars
Sets the skip chance while patched, 0V to 10V; with the menu set to binary it instead skips every evaluation while it is above 1V
Sets that channel's weight from a voltage, 0V to 10V; how far it overrides the PROB knob is set by that channel's PROB XFADE
The signal that channel passes while it is on; with nothing patched it reads the fixed voltage set on the menu, so the channel puts out a plain gate or trigger
That channel's input while the channel is on and silence while it is off, with the fade or the trigger applied, carrying as many channels as its input
A voltage for how many channels are on: their share of the tracks taking part scaled to 10V, or a fixed step per voice when the menu says so
Menu — Prob CV crossfade mode: Loose, Normal, Hard — raises every channel's weight to the power of one, two or three before the draw, so the harder settings favour the strongest weights
Menu — Beats per bar: 2 to 8 beats — sets how many clock pulses make one bar
Menu — Min active voices — sets a floor under the number of voices drawn, so an evaluation never leaves everything silent
Menu — Default input voltage: 1V (gate/trigger), 10V (CV/audio) — sets what an unpatched channel input reads, which is what that channel's output carries while it is on
Menu — Active output CV mode: Proportional to active tracks, Absolute (1.67V per voice, 6-ch scale), Absolute (0.625V per voice, 16-ch scale) — scales the OUT CH. AMOUNT jack
Menu — Skip CV mode: Probabilistic, Binary (on/off) — reads the SKIP CV jack as a chance, or as a switch that skips everything while it is above 1V
Menu — Skip mode: Global, Per channel — passes over the whole evaluation, or draws separately for each channel whether it keeps what it was doing
Menu — Trigger duration: 1ms, 2ms, 5ms, 10ms — sets the pulse length a channel in T mode sends
Menu — Reset input mode: Reset bars, Force evaluate — sets whether the RESET jack zeroes the bar count or forces an evaluation at once
Note — nothing happens until a clock is patched: evaluations are counted in clock pulses and the module has no clock of its own
Note — a channel with nothing patched into its input works as a gate or trigger source on its own, because an unpatched input reads the fixed voltage set on the menu
Note — the name beside each channel is an editable four-character label, double-clicked to type; it is drawn in its own widget, so no help line can be reached by clicking it
Note — a channel's lamp is blue in T mode waiting, white for 300ms after a trigger, green while the channel is open, yellow during a fade and red while it is closed
Note — the Maestro Expander 10 adds channels 7 to 16, and is linked from the expander's own right-click menu rather than by being placed beside this module
Note — the small red lamp by OUT CH. AMOUNT lights when the 1.67V-per-voice mode is chosen with an expander linked, where more than six active voices push that jack past 10V

Maestro.notes: The maker's README names the Prob CV crossfade modes Normal (Linear), Biased (Quadratic) and Hard (Cubic); the menu the code builds prints Loose, Normal and Hard (src/Maestro.cpp:986-1002), and Normal is the default. The README also gives two Active output CV modes where the code has three (src/Maestro.cpp:1062-1080). The weight for a channel with nothing in its Prob CV jack is the knob alone, whatever the crossfade knob is set to (src/Maestro.cpp:412-421). An evaluation is scheduled and then carried out on the following sample, so a CV arriving with the clock is read after it has settled. The six channel inputs and outputs are given no family: the maker's own summary says they carry gate, clock, audio or trigger signals, so any colour would be a guess.

lines: Arrangement structure generator for Maestro: it steps through eight sections on a clock, each with its own length, its own target density and its own weight for each of Maestro's six channels
Chooses the style within the category the STYLE switch selects; the name of the style appears in the GENRE display
Chooses which set of styles the GEN SEL knob picks from: organic, electronic or custom
Auto steps to the next section on its own when the current one has run its bars; manual holds there until a JUMP button is pressed
Loosens the section lengths: at zero a section lasts exactly its duration, and higher settings let it end up to half that many bars early or late
Scales the Blur CV input before it is added to the PART BLUR knob, and turns it upside down below the middle
Sets how many bars that section lasts: Skip, 1, 2, 4 or 8 bars, where Skip passes the section over entirely
Moves the arrangement to that section at once, in either mode, despite the manual saying a jump is held until the next bar
Counts beats on each rise above 1V; a bar is as many beats as the menu says, and section durations are counted in bars
Returns the arrangement to the first section on a rising edge above 1V, and fires the section trigger
Adds to the PART BLUR knob through the BLUR ATT. control, 0V to 10V for the full amount of blur
The whole structure on one sixteen-channel cable: density, randomness, length, blur, section number, the three triggers, a tension voltage, a protocol version and the six channel weights
The current section's target voice count, 0V to 10V standing for none to six voices, for patching to Maestro's DENS CV
Which section is playing, 0V for the first of the eight and 10V for the last
A 1ms pulse at 10V each time the arrangement moves to another section
A 1ms pulse at 10V every so many bars, the count set on the menu
A 1ms pulse at 10V when the arrangement comes back round to the first section
That channel's weight in the current section, 0V to 10V, for patching to the matching PROB CV on Maestro
Menu — Phrase trigger every: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 or 8 bars — sets how often the phrase trigger fires
Menu — Beats per bar: 2 to 8 beats — sets how many clock pulses make one bar
Menu — Part 1 — with the STYLE switch on custom, this sets that section's name, its target density, the weight for each of the six channels and the recommended voice names; one per section
Note — nothing advances without a clock: sections are counted in bars of clock pulses and the module has no clock of its own
Note — the display across the top names the voice each of Maestro's six channels is meant to carry in the current style; it is a suggestion and changes nothing in the patch
Note — a section's lamp lights while that section is playing, and the next section's lamp blinks while manual mode is held for a jump
Note — the name on each section is an editable field drawn in its own widget, so no help line can be reached by clicking it
Note — the least that has to be patched for this to drive Maestro is DENSITY CV to its DENS CV and the six channel outputs to its PROB CV jacks, with both crossfade knobs turned fully to CV
Note — the panel prints DENS CV over the column of six channel outputs, while each of them carries that channel's role weight rather than a density

SomeStructure.notes: The jump buttons act at once (src/SomeStructure.cpp:475-480), where the maker's README says they wait for the next bar boundary. The style category switch is configured Organic, Electronic, Custom (src/SomeStructure.cpp:301) with Electronic as the default, and the panel prints them CUSTOM, ELEC., ORG. from the top down. The blur calculation uses the C library's own rand() rather than a seeded generator (src/SomeStructure.cpp:510). A section whose duration is set to Skip is stepped over by a recursive call, so eight sections all set to Skip would recurse without end.

lines: Expander adding channels 7 to 16 to Maestro: ten more rows of input, probability, mode and output, tied to a Maestro chosen on this module's own right-click menu rather than by position
Sets that channel's weight in the linked Maestro's draw, 0 for never chosen and 1 for most likely
Crossfades that channel's weight between its PROB knob and its PROB CV jack: fully anticlockwise the knob alone, fully clockwise the voltage alone
Sets what that channel does when it is chosen: F fades its input up and down over the linked Maestro's fade times, G switches it through at once, T sends a short pulse
Sets that channel's weight from a voltage, 0V to 10V; how far it overrides the PROB knob is set by that channel's PROB XFADE
The signal that channel passes while it is on; with nothing patched it reads the fixed voltage set on the linked Maestro's menu
That channel's input while the channel is on and silence while it is off, with the fade or the trigger applied, carrying as many channels as its input
Menu — Link to Core: None, Core — picks which Maestro this expander adds its channels to, listing each by its module number and marking any that another expander has already claimed
Note — this module does nothing until it is linked to a Maestro from its own right-click menu: unlinked, the panel is dimmed and every output stays at 0V
Note — it can go anywhere in the rack, beside its Maestro or not, because the link is made through the menu rather than by position
Note — once linked, the Maestro's ACTIVE TRACKS control reaches 16 and its channels 7 to 16 are the rows on this panel
Note — the name beside each row is an editable label drawn in its own widget, so no help line can be reached by clicking it
Note — every decision is made by the linked Maestro, which reads these knobs and switches and writes these outputs itself; this module holds no clock, evaluation or fade of its own

MaestroExp.notes: The expander's own process() only zeroes its outputs and lamps while it is unlinked (src/MaestroExp.hpp:139-155); when linked, the Maestro reads and writes this module's params, inputs, outputs and lights inside its own process(), in the same sample. The ten channel inputs and outputs are given no family, for the same reason as the Maestro's own: they carry gate, clock, audio or trigger signals, whatever is patched. The channel labels live on the Maestro, which keeps sixteen of them whether or not an expander is linked.
